messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: runtime-pool-4 node gpu-3 OOM spike detected. 47% p99 latency increase across /v1/generate and 12k failed token writes in the last 3m. Pager sent to oncall.

sara (oncall): I'm on it. pulling logs now — starting a timeline. first glance: several `allocation failed` entries from runtime on gpu-3.

matt: seeing the same. log tail attached, kv-cache eviction events cluster at the same time as the OOMs.

priya: can you paste the kernel oops / nvidia-smi snippet? need GPU mem usage trend.

lee: pasting snapshot from 1734212250 (approx 2m before alert):
```
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,index,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.used,memory.total --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/gpu-trace.csv
2024-04-12 16:43:20, 3, 97 %, 89 %, 40928 MiB, 49152 MiB
2024-04-12 16:44:20, 3, 99 %, 94 %, 47104 MiB, 49152 MiB
```

lee: also runtime logs show repeated `kv_cache::evict_page` spikes with pages freed ~12MB each, interleaved with `alloc failed: cudaMalloc`

omar: grabbed k8s logs:
```
kubectl -n runtime logs runtime-node-gpu-3 --since=10m | grep -i oom | tail -n 80
2024-04-12T16:44:23Z ERROR runtime::memory: allocation failed: 16777216 bytes
2024-04-12T16:44:24Z WARN runtime::kvcache: evicting page id=0x7f3a size=125M
2024-04-12T16:44:24Z ERROR runtime::scheduler: op batch_id=9835 failed due to OOM
```

omar: also noticed sudden batch-size jump in traffic around 16:43 — upstream client went from avg 8 -> 24 concurrent tokens per request (likely a ramp).

zane: hypothesis #H1: workload burst increased max sequence lengths and concurrency causing KV cache churn -> fragmentation -> cudaMalloc failures.

zane: hypothesis #H2: a recent kernel tweak (deferred free) increased fragmentation under heavy eviction patterns.

priya: quick mitigation suggestions: 1) throttle/limit per-connection batch tokens at edge 2) temporarily reduce runtime max_batch_size to 8 3) pin fallback to CPU-quantized model for non-critical customers 4) enable aggressive prefix caching for hot routes.

sara (oncall): runbook says first step: limit ingress per-route and rollout temporary async fallback. I'm enacting throttle now for the busiest route `/v1/generate`.

ops-bot: action logged: route /v1/generate throttled to 60 rps (from 200) by sara at 2024-04-12T16:45:10Z. :white_check_mark:

matt: reducing max_batch_size on runtime pool 4 to 8. patch command:
```
curl -X POST "$ORCH/api/pools/4/config" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"max_batch_size":8}'
```

matt: applied. monitoring mem pressure.

lee: sharing a small log excerpt for timeline building — please add to the shared GCS: gs://redwood-incident-logs/1734212345/live-logs.tar.gz

priya: I'm spinning up extra dedicated fallbacks for top 3 paying customers, routing them over in ~5m.

rachel: customer-impact check — initial spike affected ~4% of active sessions (errors >= 5xx), highest impact between 16:44:20 and 16:47:00. APM traces show retry storms from SDK replays.

sara (oncall): assigned owners: H1 -> zane (lead), H2 -> matt (lead). Please add hypothesis comments as you test.

zane: quick test — forced KV cache compaction on node gpu-3: `curl $RUNTIME/admin/kv/compaction?node=gpu-3` result: compaction freed ~3.2GB but OOMs persisted for ~20s after. logging hypothesis -> fragmentation not solved by compaction alone. #H1 partial

matt: after lowering batch_size we saw immediate drop in `alloc failed` incidents. counts: before=120 OOMs/min, after=8 OOMs/min. Suggest this was triggering factor.

omar: collecting heap profiles and GPU allocation traces, pushing to GCS path: gs://redwood-incident-traces/1734212345/gpu-allocs.trace

ops-bot: timeline entry created: {"start":"2024-04-12T16:43:00Z","alert":"OOM spike","mitigations":["throttle","batch_size_reduction","kv_compaction"],"cust_impact":"4% sessions"}

priya: note — there was a deploy 2h earlier touching the kvcache eviction policy (PR #2345). Can someone link the rollout window?

lee: PR #2345 rollout window shows 14:10-14:35 UTC, gradually to 100% earlier today. config changed `deferred_free = true` in kvcache allocator.

zane: adding hypothesis #H3: deferred_free combined with bursty eviction increases fragmentation surface area under high concurrency. plan: revert deferred_free on a canary pool and rerun load test.

matt: can confirm metric: fragmentation_ratio(node gpu-3) jumped from 0.12 -> 0.46 between 16:40 and 16:44 based on our allocator metrics (see graph link: https://grafana/redwood/d/allocs).

rachel: customer comms: prepping an update for affected customers — will state degraded latency and increased errors for ~3m window, mitigations applied. Any objections?

sara (oncall): go ahead. include note that dedicated capacity unaffected. recommend customers use Dedicated or lower latency tiers until root fix.

zane: test plan for H3: revert `deferred_free=false` on pool 4 (canary), run synthetic 3x burst for 10m. if fragmentation stays low, plan full revert.

matt: canary revert done on pool 4 at 16:54:10. monitoring.

lee: early result: canary pool fragmentation_ratio stabilized at 0.14, no OOM during synthetic burst. control pool still had intermittent OOMs.

zane: H3 looks plausible. marking H3 status: "likely".

priya: longer-term actions: 1) add fragmentation alerts to infra (fragmentation_ratio > 0.25) 2) add per-pool deferred_free rollout gating 3) increased test coverage for KV eviction patterns in stress tests.

omar: uploading all raw logs and a short RCA draft to: gs://redwood-incident-rca/1734212345/rca-draft.md

ops-bot: incident severity updated: Sev3 -> moved to RCA tracking. Incident timeline saved.

rachel: final note for customer impact doc: affected window 16:43:20 - 16:47:00 UTC, ~4% sessions affected, root cause likely allocator config change interacting with bursty traffic causing KV cache fragmentation and cudaMalloc failures. mitigation: throttles + batch_size reduction + revert deferred_free on canary -> full revert scheduled after validation.

sara (oncall): closing live mitigation. follow-up: H3 full rollback in 2h if no regressions, FR (follow-up review) scheduled tomorrow 10:30 local. great triage team, please add any missing logs to the GCS paths. :thumbsup:
